summary: What: Project S.P.H.E.R.E. (Spatial Positioning Harmonic Empirical Resonance Experiment), operated by SPHERE Research, LLC, is a staged experimental research program subjecting unconventional, source-inspired hypotheses to conventional metrology, uncertainty analysis, controls, preregistration, and independent replication.

Phase 1 (LOC-1): a theory-neutral differential mechanical-resonance experiment testing for a reproducible position-associated residual in a thin-walled hollow copper sphere under controlled conditions. A detected residual requires investigation rather than establishing a mechanism.
Status: pre-results readiness and qualification stage. Protocol LOC-1 is registered on OSF; no physical measurements have been taken and no funds have been raised.
Where to start: the registered LOC-1 protocol, Whitepaper v2.0, and the FAQ.
Project S.P.H.E.R.E. is a staged experimental research program operated by SPHERE Research, LLC (Delaware LLC, Rochester, NY). It does not assume its motivating hypotheses are correct.

Phase 1 (LOC-1) tests for a position-associated mechanical-resonance residual in a hollow copper sphere. The motivating >230 kHz figure and 3–4 inch sphere concept are source-inspired starting points, not recognized physical thresholds; final geometry and mode are subject to FEM and qualification.
Pre-results status: no measurements have been collected, and independent tracks (Phase 2 extensions and ANT-B-01) remain proposed and separate from registered LOC-1.
Protocol LOC-1 is officially registered and live on OSF; that immutable registration governs confirmatory Phase 1 analysis unless formally amended before data inspection.
The controlled technical specification is published in Whitepaper Version 2.0 (superseding Version 1.0 archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23583932).
Proposed metrology refinements are documented separately as Draft Amendment LOC-1A; Phase 2 extensions and ANT-B-01 do not amend registered LOC-1. No measurements or results exist.
SPHEREVL (the Control Room) is a Level 0 educational simulation of the proposed S.P.H.E.R.E. measurement workflow.
It contains no physical measurements, is not a validated digital twin, and cannot confirm or refute any physical hypothesis.
This page documents the public repository facts, capability maturity level, and intended-use boundaries of the simulator.

faqs.question: Does SPHEREVL show real measurements?
faqs.answer: No. SPHEREVL is a Level 0 educational simulation of the proposed laboratory workflow. It displays synthetic model output and is not physical measurement data or scientific validation.

faqs.question: Can SPHEREVL confirm the locational-variable hypothesis or validate an anomaly?
faqs.answer: No. A simulator cannot confirm a physical hypothesis, and low simulated noise settings do not make a displayed difference genuine. Only qualified, blinded, pre-registered, and independently replicated physical measurements could evaluate a candidate residual.
